##### 3.4 Analysis of thermal energy distribution 

Cooling is the first important step in the smelter gas treatment chain, prior to dust precipitation and sulphur recovery. Recovering heat and converting it to power is an important factor but not always the primary reason for using WHB for gas cooling. The most important reason is eliminating extreme operating temperatures and provid

ing conditions for desired chemical reactions for dust and gas components (sulphatation of dust) and simultaneously minimizing unwanted reactions (excess conversion to SO3). This is done by constructing the WHB steam pressure and saturation temperature ‘window’ above acid dew point, but below material temperature limitation or dust sticking range [6]. Heat transfer in WHB is quite complex due to the varying gas velocity and temperature requirements for the radiation and convection zones. Radiation is influenced by the radiative surface and medium characteristics and also by the gas velocity. It is preferred to have slow motion (low velocity, longer flow path, higher mixing) of gas to maximize the surface to surface heat transfer in this section. Heat transfer in the convection section is forced convection and is enhanced by the higher gas velocities. This, along with the constraint of maintaining the radiation outlet temperature <700o C, convection outlet temperature <350o C and optimal sulphation reactions temperature range of 500-800o C was the focus of the comparative heat transfer analysis of the various design modifications attempted. _Proceedings of Copper 2010_ 2510 _Design Modification Using CFD to Improve the Performance of the Waste Heat Boiler_ (B)

#### 4 Summary 

The Reaction shaft-settler-uptake shaft-WHB design configuration creates a high swirling, n

onuniform flow with biasness towards the left wall and a severe short-circuiting along the roof for the unmodified WHB. Sulphation air flow from all the nozzles show inefficient penetration and shortcircuiting along with the main gas. 

The flow distribution improves with modified nozzles; the high velocity sulphation air breaks the main gas flow jet improving its mixing with main gas resulting in an increased residence times in the radiation zone. 

Flow pattern is influenced by the length of the baffle. An improved uniform and lower intensity flow with reduced impact on the roof and side walls is observed as a result of the baffle. Although altered due to the baffle, the flow pattern adheres to the gas flow path of the unmodified design for the short baffle. Flow becomes almost comparatively straight at the throat with large recirculation near baffle for the long baffle design. 

The effect of gas flow path and velocity is observed on heat transfer. Designs without baffle show underutilized lower radiation zone for heat transfer. The reduced gas velocity and altered flow path improves the temperature distribution for the baffle designs. The effective sulphation temperature improves considerably in the radiation chamber with the baffle designs. 

Design modifications with short baffle provides an optimal design with respect to flow uniformity and reduced flow intensity, improved mixing of off-gas and sulphation air, enhanced cooling, desired temperature range for sulphation reaction and lower recirculation near baffle. 

An improved boiler performance as a result of baffle implementation, boiler revamping and improved operational practice was observed.

Aurubis has, with the support of Clyde Materials Handling (“CMH”), developed a low energy, low maintenance, and highly reliable pneumatic conveying system capable of transporting copper concentrate from the drying facilities to the concentrate bin. This system has been providing optimal operation for Aurubis for over four years. 

Aurubis required the pneumatic conveying expertise of CMH to replace unreliable, high energy consuming mechanical technologies that were unable to provide the sufficient levels of productivity and availability sought. 

This paper will discuss the process and mate

rial handling challenges, which Aurubis and CMH solved together, as well as highlighting the operational, economic and environmental benefits, this system has generated.

#### 3 Challenges Faced 

Aurubis’ existing copper concentrate conveying system utilised two in line drag chain conveyors and from this directly to an air lift delivering to the day bin. Unfortunately these systems were breaking down with increasing frequency, and as a consequence, driving up maintenance times and costs, which were impacting on production. The mechanical systems are susceptible to fine materials, which damage bearings and with age, this can lead to repeated failure. 

In an effort to overcome these issues, Aurubis sought a low energy, low maintenance solution to ensure that operating costs were reduced to a minimum and that increased availability was created in an effort to maximise productivity. Clyde Materials Handling was given the opportunity to resolve these issues for Aurubis through the implementation of pneumatic conveying systems. 

The first system, a 50 ton per hour (tph) copper concentrate system, was to be delivered and installed within a 16 week timeframe, with the installation target time to be completed in a 25 hour period, with the existing mechanical drag chain conveyor still in operation. The second 120-tph system was also to be delivered in a 16-week timeframe, with the installation target time to be completed in 48 hours. The installation of both systems would have to be implemented in Aurubis’ existing pit located below their steam dryers. Each system had a 120 metre route with a double lift out of the pit and then up to the day bin itself a 50 m lift. The materials comprising of Copper Concentrate, Silica and Reverts are mixed and then dried. This very abrasive mixture exits the dryer and enters the conveying system at 120 °C. 

The scope of supply would incorporate buffer hoppers with aeration system, pneumatic conveying vessels, conveying pipelines with ceramic bends, terminal boxes, control systems, screw air compressors and staff training in operating and maintaining the system. 

Both copper concentrate systems would be created by CMH utilising pneumatic conveying technology. 

#### 4 Prйcis of Pneumatic Conveying 

Pneumatic conveying is, generally, the most efficient and effective method of transporting granular and bulk solid materials to storage, or to process within a production environment. There are three forms of pneumatic conveying that Clyde has expertise within, namely, Dense Phase, Medium Phase and Lean Phase, positive and negative pressure pneumatic conveying. 

Dense Phase solutions are suitable for transportin

g difficult, abrasive or friable materials. This method of conveying pushes material along a pipeline in a plug flow at relatively low velocity (2-8 metres per second). This mode of conveying results in minimal wear on pipelines and bends, promoting minimum maintenance and long life on system components. Efficient use of compressed air also generates low power consumption and reduced operating costs. Dense Phase Pneumatic Conveying technologies move material in an energy efficient and environmentally supportive man-

The findings of the testing and data from other sites were taken into consideration when deploying the systems for Aurubis’ Hamburg operation. Close contact with Aurubis ensured these considerations were fully understood and met all expectations for the design and deployment phase of the project.

#### Abstract 

Over the past one year of industrial production, the new bath smelting process developed at the Fangyuan Non-Ferrous Metal, having higher oxygen enrichment, high throughput, high oxygen pressure, high negative pressure, has shown many advantages, such as high lance life and high efficiency of pyretic smelting. Matte grade can be easily controlled, as required. The environmental condition of the new process is no dust and off-gas. This paper gives a brief description of the new process and its feature mentioned above. It also certifies the feasibility of the new oxygen enrichment bottom-blowing bath smelting process based on the common metallurgical theory of bath smelting process. 

The author of the paper summarizes the whole production period in which oxygen-enriched bottomblowing smelting process is used and presents some problems for discussion. 

#### 1 Introduction 

The Fangyuan Non-Ferrous Company, which was founded in 1998, is located in Dongying City, Shandong Province, China. The company has produced electrolytic copper from copper scrap since 1998. The production capability is 200,000 tons per year. By the end of 2008, a new smelter with 100,000 tons blister copper per year was started. The technology adopted is high level of oxygenenriched bottom-blowing bath smelting of matte, P-S converter blowing, anode furnace refining. The heat of off-gas from the bottom-blowing furnace and converter furnace is reclaimed, after precipitation, the gas is used for making sulfuric acid to recover SO2 in it. The steam produced by a waste heat boiler is used to generate electricity. 

The oxygen used for the bottom-blowing furnace is made by a self-built oxygen generation station, which adopts 10 kNm<sup>3</sup> /h deep cooling. The oxygen-enriched bottom-blowing smelting process is

#### 2 Process flowsheet introduction: oxygen-enriched bottom-blowing smelting process 

Mixed materials without drying and milling are continuously transported by a belt conveyor into a high temperature melt in the furnace through the feed mouth. Oxygen and air are blown constantly by the oxygen lance into melting copper matte, in which iron and sulfur are rapidly oxidized as well as slag is formed. Sulfur dioxide produced is directed through the waste-heat boiler and electric precipitation, then led into the acid plant to form sulfuric acid. Slag formed in the furnace can be tapped regularly through a taphole at the end of the furnace, lifted by a ladle to the slag site for slow cooling, followed by the slag flotation mill. Co

pper matte formed in the furnace is tapped regularly through a taphole on the middle part of one side of the furnace, lifted by a ladle into the P-S converter. Figure 1 shows a new process flowsheet for oxygen-enriched bottom-blowing bath smelting.

#### 3 Main equipment of the bottom-blowing furnace 

The main equipment is a horizontal rotating furnace of the size Φ 4.4Ч16.5 m, which is lined with 380 mm thick chrome-magnesite bricks, similar to the Noranda furnace in outline. The difference between them is that oxygen is blown by tuyeres in the Noranda furnace while in the bottomblowing furnace it is blown by an oxygen lance. The bottom blowing furnace has 9 oxygen lances, which are arranged in two rows; the low row with 5 lances sloping towards the outside furnace at 7°, the upper row with 4 lances towards the outside furnace at 22°, the separation angle between the two rows is 15°. The oxygen plant facing the furnace has a capability of 10,000 Nm<sup>3</sup> /h oxygen supply using a deep cooling system. The off-gas system can be treated 120,000 Nm<sup>3</sup> /h gas, which corresponds with the acid plant. In addition, there are 3 converters of the size Φ 3.8Ч8.1 m each, a corresponding waste heat boiler, an electric precipitation system as well as slag flotation mill.

#### 6 The basic theory of bottom-blowing bath smelting process 

##### 6.1 The common metallurgical theory of bath smelting process 

Raw materials that are not pre-dried, milled, granulated are directly put into the furnace, which is full of high temperatur

e gas-liquid-solid in the bath. Soon the materials are melted. Oxidizing and reducing reaction, slag and matte-making take place, grains of slag and matte crush each other and then enter separately into the slag phase and matte phase, which are formed before. 

The author of the paper made a number of calculations including the melt rotating speed, cycle speed, Reynolds number, Nusselt number and Froude number. All data show that they fully comply with the requirements of the chemical reaction. 

##### 6.2 Theoretical characteristics of bottom blowing 

The so-called bottom blowing actually means blowing the matte layer. As we know, the liquidity of matte is 50-125 times higher than that of slag. Since Re=dp·vave·ρ/µ, when other conditions remain the same, Reynolds number is much higher when bottom blowing is used, many other corresponding parameters are also much superior than that of other smelting techniques. 

When bottom blowing, gas is rising upward in the melt and is divided into numerous bubbles that form a maximum contact surface between the gas and liquid phases. Because of better dynamics reaction condition, chemical reactions proceed rapidly, melt is over-heated, which leads to slagmatte separation quickly. 

During gas bubbles going upward, a “pump” function appears, and the moving energy gradually disappears, so noise caused by oxygen-enriched blowing around the furnace cannot be heard. 

The difference between the oxygen lance and tuyere. Diameter of gas flow from the lance entries into melt is about 1/10 that of the tuyere. Gas bubble volume is small, staying in melt and forming a large volume of “milk liquid”. When bottom blowing, the gas volume suspended is one third of the melt volume, while in side blowing the gas volume is only 19 % of the melt volume in the Noranda reactor.

Furthermore, oxygen enriched first enters matte layer to take part in the chemical reaction, and when oxygen enriched enters the slag layer, its oxygen voltage declines distinctly. #### 8 Conclusion 

Up to now, the new oxygen-enriched bottom-blowing bath smelting process has developed an advanced process for copper, which is more mature and improved. It possesses advantages of low investment and low production cost. The new oxygen-enriched bottom-blowing bath smelting process should become the first choice of non-ferrous metallurgical plants for process equipment improving and modification.

We believe that after constant improving, the new oxygen-enriched bottom-blowing bath smelting process will show more powerful superiority.
